answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can transact, like saffron kept under seal until its quality is proven. The bond is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating identities or spamming, so a vine of fake accounts each needs its own deposit. Creating a thousand sybils then costs a thousand bonds, turning a free attack into one priced in real capital, while honest agents get their stake back.
